thread:
maya: quick flag - enabling activation checkpointing (remat) on the 2pp/4tp nightly job caused tail latency and median token latency to jump. batch=4 run on 8xA100, observed ~17% median increase vs baseline without remat. wondering if anyone has seen comm amplification with remat + kvcache enabled :thinking:
anthony: can you paste the nsys/torch profiler summary? my gut says we might be turning previously staggered allreduces into synchronized spikes when recompute boundaries align across pipeline stages
maya: pasted a tiny nsys summary below from the failing run (trimmed):

```
# nsys summary (8 GPUs aggregated)
wall_time: 5200 ms
compute_kernels: 3120 ms
allreduce_total: 1120 ms   # baseline was ~640 ms
overlap_comm_compute: 12%  # previously ~48%
kv_cache_lookup_time: 180 ms (per-batch amortized)
```

sophia: wow allreduce almost doubled. did remat change per-rank gradient bucket sizes? remat can change activation lifetime and trigger different autograd bucket boundaries
maya: yep suspected that — we also saw the number of allreduce ops increase ~1.9x in the profiler (lots of small allreduces instead of few big ones). looks like checkpointing split a bunch of gradient buckets and the NCCL overhead dominates now
anthony: that matches. small allreduces -> higher per-call latency and worse bandwidth utilization. two levers: 1) regroup buckets (bigger bucket_size) 2) try asynchronous overlapping (use separate stream for c10d requests)
ciara-bot: triggered perf-regression-alert: job/nightly/pp2-tp4-remat — ticket #INF-3142
infra-bot: allocated debug nodes (8xA100) for reproduction, expires in 6h

maya: things I tried so far: changed autograd.buckets to 1e9 (coalesce), set torch.distributed.bucket_cap_mb=512, and ran again — allreduce count dropped and bandwidth improved, but end-to-end latency still +8% vs no-remat (so not full fix)
sophia: interesting. could be interaction with KV cache. If remat changes per-layer execution ordering, the runtime may be missing prefix/KV cache reuse and cause more KV writes or cache invalidations. do we have traces for KV cache hits during these runs?
maya: attached simplified KV trace: hits=92%, evictions spiked ~20% at step boundaries where remat boundaries align. looks like extra memory pressure during recompute phases pushes some entries out and causes re-writes
anthony: eviction + extra allreduces = double whammy. Two followups: 1) try smaller remat granularity (checkpoint every N layers) to reduce peak memory swing, 2) stagger remat boundaries across pipeline stages so allreduces don't co-occur. we can also try NCCL tuning: set NCCL_ALGO=Tree or enable COLLNET for large messages 

maya: quick diff I ran to stagger boundaries (naive): shift remat start index by rank % pp_size. patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4828 — small script in repo to produce stagger schedule

sophia: nice. any perf after staggering?
maya: preliminary: allreduce_total down from 1120 -> 760 ms, overlap up to ~34%, e2e latency now +3% vs baseline. still not perfect but big improvement. kv-evictions also fell to ~6% spike vs 20%
anthony: promising. also consider changing kernel selection for the heavy layers — if recompute causes repeated matmul reruns, using fused GEMM kernels with better cache reuse reduces recompute cost and reduces time that gradients sit pending (thus fewer concurrent allreduces). Have we tried the new fused kernel flag?
maya: flipped FLAG_USE_FUSED_MATMUL=1 in runtime config and reran single-stage perf: compute_kernels dropped ~18% but interestingly allreduce_total dropped another ~30 ms because compute finished earlier and overlap increased
sophia: sounds like a good multi-pronged fix: (A) stagger remat boundaries, (B) increase bucket cap to coalesce small allreduces, (C) enable fused matmul kernels, (D) tweak KV cache policy to prioritize retention across remat phases. We should run an automated sweep across those axes

manual-run: command used to repro:
```
python perf/run_infer.py \
  --pp 2 --tp 4 --batch 4 --remat True --kv_cache True \
  --bucket-cap-mb 512 --fused-matmul True \
  --stagger-remat True
```

anthony: also log nccl metrics: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 — we saw different algorithms chosen depending on message shapes

maya: open questions: should runtime provide a remat-aware bucketizer that groups gradients by future allreduce schedule? or we just document recommended knobs? writing an RFC would help
sophia: RFC SGTM. propose short-term runtime heuristics: detect remat enabled -> automatically increase default bucket_cap_mb and enable staggered-remat-by-rank. Long-term: remat-aware bucketizer + async allreduce queue on separate streams
anthony: I'll volunteer to prototype async-c10d stream impl. maya can you file INF-3142 with reproduction steps, perf artifacts (nsys) and the PR link?
maya: filed INF-3142 and attached traces + PR link. assigning next steps: anthony (async allreduce prototype), sophia (RFC for heuristics & kvcache retention policy), maya (sweep + perf artifacts). thanks all :thumbsup:
ciara-bot: note: meeting suggested — perf sync 10am PT tomorrow to triage and schedule rollout canary
maya: agreed, adding agenda: reproduce baseline, run staggered-remat canary, validate KV retention. see you tomorrow.
